blockers.quote: Only you can turn it. So you give away the number: the town writes it, the dial follows the napkin, and you keep the turning, knowing every renter in town would walk the moment you touched it.
blockers.why: Check #21, close the loopholes on screen: nothing prevents you secretly lowering the dial later; renters would benefit rather than walk.
blockers.fix: Replace the action and line with the phone locked in a town-hall box requiring three keys held by Marco, the rival and the mayor: "Only you can turn it. But they decide when you can reach it. The town writes the number; three keys open the box; you turn the dial in public."

blockers.quote: > SCENE: The door chimes. The steel customer, the one that paid with your card, back from the truck with a cap on, walks to the till, points at a burger to go and taps a card. Insert on the card: not yours. A colour you've never seen, no name on it. The till pings. Your phone, on the counter beside the till, does not.
blockers.why: No new power rule after halfway: the machine suddenly possesses independent money, directly reversing the established rule that it can only pay with your card.
blockers.fix: Keep this as an unanswered sequel possibility: the customer raises the unfamiliar card toward the till, but cut before it touches. Do not let the till ping or the customer receive the burger.

blockers.quote: She's right too. In 1900 about 41 percent of American workers were on farms. A century later, under 2 percent (c10). The new jobs came because people were still better at something. Here, whatever the new job is, somebody types it in.
blockers.why: Check #7, misconception first: several numbers and the explanation arrive together, violating the one-number-at-a-time requirement and weakening one-watch clarity.
blockers.fix: Split it around the assistant gag: "At the start of the last century, about forty-one percent of American workers farmed (c10)." After the machine appears: "By its end, under two percent did (c10). New jobs came because people still had something machines could not do. Here, somebody types that job in."

suggestions.quote: So, would you have turned the dial? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
suggestions.fix: Point the question at the unresolved final image: "Whose money was on that card? Tell us in the comments."

suggestions.quote: He won't, the hairdresser won't, and everyone else is in the app by Friday.
suggestions.fix: Strengthen the turn: "He won't. The hairdresser won't. But by Friday, everyone else has rented one of your machines."

suggestions.quote: You'd think a boss who doubled his workers' pay had lost his mind. In 1914 Henry Ford announced a five-dollar day, doubling his workers' pay (c16), and wrote later that his own sales depended, in a measure, on the wages he paid, because that money gets spent with storekeepers and distributors (c17).
suggestions.fix: After the fact, show it causing the next beat: you copy Ford's sales line beneath Marco's missing line, then call the owners' meeting.

keep.quote: What if you fired everyone and hired AI? Six weeks from now, you're the richest person this town has ever had. And its last customer.
You didn't fire a cook. You fired a customer who happened to know how to cook.
You're still the richest person in town. You just stopped being its only customer.
